title: Why your Windows update is so big: 1,400+ flaws fixed in one month
description:
In October 2026, Microsoft's Patch Tuesday fixed more than 1,400 security flaws in a single month - a record. Depending on who counted, the total is between 1,411 and 1,417. A year earlier, October 2025 had 180. That one month beat Microsoft's total for the whole of 2025.

Why so many? Microsoft's security team (MSRC) says AI-assisted research now contributes to vulnerability discovery, and update packages are addressing more and more CVEs. At least one of October's flaws, CVE-2026-96951 in Windows Shell, was already being exploited: it lets a crafted file skip the warning Windows normally shows for downloaded files.

Analyst note: a bigger update does not mean Windows got worse. It means more holes are being found and closed. Microsoft's own guidance: for many customers, the priority is to install security updates as soon as possible.

Do this tonight: open Settings, then Windows Update. Click Check for updates. Restart when asked.

Sources
- Microsoft MSRC, "Using risk cohorts to prioritize security updates" (Oct 13, 2026): https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/msrc/blog/2026/10/using-risk-cohorts-to-prioritize-security-updates
- BleepingComputer, October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,411 flaws: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-october-2026-patch-tuesday-fixes-1-411-flaws-3-zero-days/
- Infosecurity Magazine (Oct 14, 2026): https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/microsoft-patch-tuesday-record-1/
